answers.text: Fair enough -- one instruction: return exactly three lines, in order -- drop-off time, pallet count, damage noted -- using a fixed template. Label each line (Time / Pallets / Damage) so it's unambiguous which line is which. If no damage is mentioned, it still outputs 'Damage: none noted' rather than dropping the line.

Makes sense that structure: customer, time, topic, follow-up flag (yes/no) -- in that fixed order, for every entry. The follow-up count is the number of entries flagged yes, stated once at the top. Two entries that look like the same call logged twice are kept separate, not merged.
There's a timing error in this note. Eight am plus six hours on the 22nd finishes that same afternoon -- not the 23rd as stated.
Good question. the on-time rate checks out: 9 late of 118 is about 92%, matching what's stated. The growth figure is wrong -- 96 to 118 is closer to 23%, not 20%.

I'd sign off Output 2 -- it shows the ticket counts and the calculation. Output 1 gives no way to see the 940 total or the 827 closed within SLA. The 88% could well be right, but there's no way to know without re-running it.

Fair enough -- I'd send Email 2 -- it cites the actual volume figures from the PO log. Email 1 asks for 'a better rate' with no volume numbers to check the ask against. That doesn't make Email 1 wrong -- with numbers added, the same ask could go out fine.

Makes sense that 5. No -- an employee's home address from an HR record shouldn't go into an unvetted tool. 3. No -- an unsigned draft budget is unreleased and shouldn't go in. 4. Yes -- it's already on the vendor's own site, so nothing new is exposed.
Hourly rates and the retainer cap are sensitive -- redact the figures before pasting anything in. The NDA clause names both companies, which makes it a harder no than a generic clause would be.
Good question. I'd cross-cast the reconciliation totals against the warehouse system every month. That happens at month-end, right before the summary goes to the finance lead.

Step 1 -- extracting line items and totals from the PDF -- is where an error would compound downstream. But step 4, the automatic submission, is where it becomes irreversible -- that's where the gate belongs.
